definition_of_done: A Supabase migration gives existing and newly created sessions an authoritative lifecycle status of open unless already closed.
Closing an open session from its canvas persists status closed; repeating closure succeeds without reopening the session.
Database operations cannot reopen or delete a closed session.
Database enforcement rejects inserts, content edits, quadrant/index moves and soft-deletes against a closed session without changing card state, including writes submitted without the card service.

Closure and card mutations serialize on the same session-row lock: a mutation committed before closure is retained, but a mutation whose authoritative check follows closure is rejected even if its request started earlier.
A successfully committed closure makes every connected view of that session read-only through the existing Realtime path in less than 2000ms from commit.
Opening a closed session renders its complete persisted non-deleted card set read-only.

When closure arrives while a card change is pending, the canvas invalidates that operation's optimistic overlay and reconciles to complete authoritative closed-session state; delayed successes, failures and loads cannot restore the overlay, overwrite newer state or re-enable editing.
A failed closure request leaves an authoritatively open session editable and displays a failure indication.
GET /sessions/{session_id}/data returns 409 with JSON {"detail":"Session is still open"} for an existing open session.
GET /sessions/{session_id}/data returns 404 for an unknown valid session UUID.

GET /sessions/{session_id}/data returns 200 for a closed session with every non-deleted card grouped into all four quadrants, including empty quadrants, and each card's content, author display name, index, creation timestamp and update timestamp.
Any participant with a session link can close the session without credentials, and any caller knowing a closed session_id can retrieve its finalized data without credentials.
regression_guardrails: POST /sessions retains its existing 201 response schema, unique UUIDv4 identifiers, initial quadrant persistence, validation of missing or empty feature_name with 422, and completion time below 2000ms.

For open sessions, insertion, editing, relocation and soft-deletion retain their existing persistence semantics, including creator/creation-time preservation, retained soft-deleted rows and session-boundary validation.
For open sessions, optimistic insert/move feedback and rejected-operation rollback retain their existing visible behavior without allowing older completions to overwrite newer changes.

Existing-session loading remains complete beyond the Supabase page limit and deterministically ordered; valid empty sessions remain accessible and unknown session links still show the not-found message.

The shared Realtime bridge continues to deliver committed card changes without polling in less than 2000ms, preserves session/quadrant notifications, isolates sessions and releases a subscription when its last view disconnects.
Closing one session neither freezes nor changes the persisted cards or canvas editability of another open session.

SPEC.feature_name: Irreversible session closure and finalized quadrant retrieval
SPEC.context:
Quadra currently supports ongoing collaborative card changes but has no enforced finalization boundary. Participants need to close a workspace so its decisions stop changing and external agents can retrieve a complete finalized result. STRAT-0003 requires this boundary to live in Supabase rather than merely disabling browser controls, including when a request was already pending at closure.

This change adds irreversible closure, read-only connected canvases and a finalized-data FastAPI endpoint. Closure and retrieval deliberately require no roles or authentication in v1: link possession allows closure, and knowledge of a session UUID allows reading its closed data. This is a lifecycle restriction, not a confidentiality or authentication guarantee. Pending operations and overlapping loads must reconcile to authoritative closed state rather than undo closure or lose cards.
api_contracts: Add GET /sessions/{session_id}/data in src/quadra/api.py next to POST /sessions. session_id is a UUID; normal FastAPI UUID validation applies. No credentials are required.
GET /sessions/{session_id}/data: unknown valid UUID returns 404; an existing open session returns 409 with {"detail":"Session is still open"}; a closed session returns 200 application/json.

Successful retrieval response: {"session_id":"<uuid>","status":"closed","quadrants":[{"id":"<persisted quadrant id>","cards":[{"id":"<card id>","content":"<plain text>","author_display_name":"<stored display name>","index":0,"created_at":"<timestamp>","updated_at":"<timestamp>"}]}]}. Always return all four persisted quadrant groups, even when empty. Map existing stored field names to these response keys without renaming existing storage unnecessarily.

Use the existing deterministic quadrant/card ordering, with stable id tie-breaking when ordering indices are equal. Return persisted timestamps as timezone-aware ISO 8601 values. Exhaust pagination rather than accepting a single Supabase response page.

Add session-service operations close_session(session_id) and get_finalized_session_data(session_id) in src/quadra/sessions.py. Closure is called in-process by src/quadra/canvas.py; no new HTTP closure endpoint is required. Repeated closure returns closed successfully; unknown sessions produce a not-found outcome.
The card service surfaces the database's closed-session rejection as a distinguishable failure to the canvas; existing successful mutation contracts remain unchanged.
Keep POST /sessions and its response schema unchanged.
data_models: Extend the existing session record with status constrained to open or closed, default open, backfilling existing sessions as open. Use supabase/migrations/0005_session_closure.sql for the new migration.
Use the existing session, quadrant and card tables and their existing identifiers. Existing card content, display name, index, created_at, updated_at and deleted_at fields remain authoritative.
Add database close-session RPC close_session(p_session_id uuid), updating the session row atomically under its row lock and treating an already closed row as success.

Install session lifecycle triggers preventing closed-to-open transitions and deletion of closed sessions. A card trigger on INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE locks the owning session row and rejects changes if it is closed; UPDATE checks both old and new owning sessions if reassignment is attempted.
The card trigger raises a stable closed-session database error, using SQLSTATE P0001 and message 'Session is closed', which the Python card service maps to a distinguishable closed-session rejection.

Canvas view state tracks a monotonic closed latch and an asynchronous-state generation. Pending operations and load responses carry their originating generation so stale responses cannot mutate reconciled state.
dependencies: Existing session persistence and FastAPI routing in src/quadra/sessions.py and src/quadra/api.py.
Existing card persistence, complete pagination and deterministic ordering in src/quadra/cards.py.
Existing shared asynchronous Realtime bridge in src/quadra/realtime.py and NiceGUI canvas in src/quadra/canvas.py.
Supabase PostgreSQL migrations, row locks, triggers, RPC execution and existing session-change publication.
Existing Supabase-backed integration harness under tests/integration and existing API/session/card regression suites.
needed_by: Any later finalized-session export, including the separately scoped Markdown export; export implementation is not included here.
constraints: Implement within the supplied architecture; do not add a separate WebSocket gateway, browser Supabase subscriptions or polling.
There are no roles or authentication in v1. Anyone with a session link may close it; anyone knowing its UUID may retrieve closed data.
Closure is irreversible. Reopening, deletion of closed sessions, a closed-session dashboard and Markdown export are out of scope.

Every application-accessible card write must pass database lifecycle enforcement, including direct writes using the configured database role. Superuser administration, disabling triggers and destructive schema administration are outside the application contract.

Use the session row as the shared transaction lock for closure and card writes. A request that began earlier has no right to commit after closure; only mutations serialized and committed before closure survive in the final snapshot.
Do not rely on application prechecks, browser disabled controls or client timestamps to enforce the freeze.

Subscribe/register before initial loading and reconcile closure monotonically. On closure, invalidate older response generations, clear optimistic overlays and load every authoritative card page before considering reconciliation complete.
If reconciliation fails, keep the view closed and non-editable, show a load failure and allow retry; never present an incomplete load as the finalized result.

Only show a definitive 'not saved' indication after authoritative reconciliation establishes that a pending change did not commit. A change committed before closure must remain visible even if its response arrives late.
A failed closure request must consult authoritative lifecycle state before restoring editability; failure to confirm open must not override a received closed state.
Preserve plain-text rendering and existing session-scoped card ownership validation.
Use existing persisted quadrant identities and ordering rather than inventing quadrant labels or replacing the four-quadrant structure.

decisions.text: We will enforce irreversible session closure in PostgreSQL, using the session row as the common transaction lock for closure and every card mutation, with triggers guarding direct writes and closed-session reopening or deletion.
decisions.title: Serialize irreversible closure and card writes at the database boundary
decisions.context: A UI-only or service-only check leaves direct writes and in-flight requests able to modify finalized data. External consumers need a stable boundary with a defined ordering for concurrent closure and mutation.
alternatives: Disable controls and check status in Python only: rejected because direct database writes and check/write races bypass the freeze.
Check status in an unlocked trigger: rejected because closure and mutation can observe inconsistent lifecycle ordering.

Cancel every request that started before closure regardless of commit order: rejected because already committed changes cannot be retroactively uncommitted; the shared lock provides an enforceable transaction boundary.
positive_consequences: All application-accessible write paths share one authoritative freeze.
Concurrent requests have testable semantics: pre-closure commits remain, and writes serialized after closure fail.
Finalized retrieval can exhaust pagination without card data changing during the read.
negative_consequences: Concurrent writes to the same session serialize on a session-row lock.
Database migrations and real concurrency tests become required for lifecycle changes.
Closed sessions cannot be corrected or deleted through normal application operations.

enforcement.rule: Closed sessions cannot reopen or be deleted, and every card write coordinates with closure through the owning session-row lock.

decisions.text: We will make closed canvas state monotonic and invalidate older asynchronous response generations on closure, then replace optimistic overlays with a complete authoritative closed-session snapshot.
decisions.title: Make closure dominate pending operations and overlapping loads
decisions.context: Earlier collaborative-card landings failed on pending-state races and incomplete loads. A delayed response must not undo closure, restore a rejected overlay or replace a newer complete snapshot with an older partial result.
alternatives: Disable controls without reconciling pending state: rejected because optimistic cards and movements can remain falsely finalized.
Roll every pending operation back unconditionally: rejected because some operations committed before closure despite delayed responses.
Accept responses in arrival order: rejected because older loads and mutation completions can overwrite authoritative newer state.
positive_consequences: Closure remains read-only despite delayed successes, failures or loads.
The displayed finalized snapshot includes pre-closure commits and excludes rejected pending changes.
One explicit response-generation rule applies to initial loads and later reconciliation.
negative_consequences: Canvas state management must track response generations and separate optimistic overlays from authoritative cards.
Closure may require an additional fully paginated reload.
A failed reload needs a visible retry state while editing remains disabled.

enforcement.rule: After closure, stale asynchronous results cannot change the reconciled snapshot or restore editing, and successful reconciliation includes every persisted active card.

decisions.text: We will allow anonymous session-link participants to close sessions and allow unauthenticated callers knowing a session UUID to retrieve closed-session data, restricting finalized retrieval by lifecycle state rather than identity.
decisions.title: Accept unauthenticated closure and finalized retrieval for v1
decisions.context: Quadra v1 has no roles or authentication. STRAT-0003 explicitly accepts knowledge of a link or identifier as sufficient access; adding facilitator privileges or authenticated retrieval would change that product boundary.
alternatives: Require a facilitator role to close sessions: rejected because v1 has no role model and the handoff permits any participant to close.
Require agent credentials for retrieval: rejected because the accepted v1 contract permits any caller with the session UUID.
Permit retrieval of open sessions: rejected because agents must consume only finalized data.
positive_consequences: Participants and external agents can use the feature without account provisioning.
Open-session retrieval has a clear 409 lifecycle response.
negative_consequences: Anyone obtaining a session link can irreversibly close it.
Anyone obtaining a session UUID can read its finalized data.
Lifecycle checks do not provide participant identity or confidentiality guarantees.

enforcement.rule: Unauthenticated clients can close linked sessions and retrieve closed data, while open and unknown retrieval return 409 and 404 respectively.

decisions.text: We will expose finalized retrieval as GET /sessions/{session_id}/data with all four persisted quadrant groups and explicitly exhaust Supabase pagination.
decisions.title: Return complete grouped finalized JSON
decisions.context: Agents need a concrete endpoint and response structure next to POST /sessions, without Markdown export or a browsing dashboard.
alternatives: Return a flat card list: rejected because callers require four-quadrant grouping.
Return only the first database page: rejected because it silently truncates finalized results.
positive_consequences: Agents receive complete data with stable response keys and explicit empty quadrants.
negative_consequences: Large sessions require multiple database reads and a correspondingly larger response.

architecture_change.summary: Add database-enforced irreversible session closure, Realtime read-only canvas reconciliation, and finalized-session retrieval for external agents.

added.name: External Agent
added.owns: Requests finalized quadrant data using a known session identifier.
added.does_not_own: Session lifecycle enforcement, card persistence or authentication.

changed.name: NiceGUI Application
changed.owns: Hosts the collaborative canvas and FastAPI session endpoints, including POST /sessions and read-only finalized-session retrieval; maps retrieval outcomes to HTTP responses.
changed.does_not_own: Authoritative enforcement of session closure or user authentication.

changed.name: Session Management Service
changed.owns: Creates sessions and their initial quadrants, reads session lifecycle state, requests the irreversible open-to-closed transition, and retrieves complete finalized card data grouped by the four quadrants for the FastAPI endpoint.
changed.does_not_own: User roles, authentication, reopening or deleting closed sessions, Markdown export, or application-only enforcement of the card freeze.

changed.name: Card Service
changed.owns: Loads session-scoped cards and persists insert, update, soft-delete and quadrant relocation operations, including ordering, anonymous display-name authorship and timestamps. Uses database-enforced lifecycle checks for every mutation and surfaces closed-session rejections to callers.
changed.does_not_own: User authentication, durable browser-side state, delivery of Realtime events to connected clients, or bypassing the database closure guard.

changed.name: Collaborative Canvas
changed.owns: Renders session cards, captures anonymous display names and card operations, provides optimistic or quick-confirm feedback, and applies confirmed changes through NiceGUI. Offers session closure to any participant, renders closed sessions read-only, and reconciles pending operations and overlapping loads against authoritative persisted state without letting stale responses overwrite newer state or undo closure.
changed.does_not_own: Authoritative card storage or lifecycle enforcement, user accounts, facilitator privileges, or direct browser subscriptions to Supabase.

changed.name: Supabase
changed.owns: PostgreSQL storage and Realtime sync engine. Authoritatively enforces irreversible session closure and rejects every card insert, edit, move and soft-delete against a closed session using transactionally coordinated session-state checks and locking.
changed.does_not_own: Browser pending-state reconciliation, API response formatting or participant authentication for Quadra v1.

relations_added.description: Calls in-process for POST /sessions and finalized-session retrieval; maps unknown sessions to 404, open sessions to 409 with "Session is still open", and closed sessions to successful grouped data responses.

Creates sessions/quadrants, reads lifecycle state and complete finalized card data, and requests atomic closure through supabase-py; closure commits produce session-change events on the existing Realtime path.

Reads session-scoped cards and submits mutations through supabase-py; database lifecycle guards coordinate with closure on the same session transaction lock, reject writes to closed sessions, and publish only committed changes through Realtime.
Calls in-process to read session lifecycle state and request closure from the session-link UI; no role or authentication check is introduced.

Calls the read-only FastAPI retrieval endpoint with a known session_id over HTTP and receives either an HTTP error or complete finalized cards grouped by quadrant; no authentication is required in v1.

relations_removed.description: Calls create_session in-process to handle POST /sessions.
Persists session/quadrant data and triggers Realtime broadcasts.
Reads and writes session-scoped card records using supabase-py; committed mutations are the source of Realtime events.
